question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 & 0\\1 & 1 & 3\\4 & 0 & k\end{bmatrix}$. If $A$ is a singular matrix, and $B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\k & 2 & 1\\1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, what is the sum of all possible values of $\det(B)$?
explanation:
Since $A$ is singular, $|A| = 0$.

$|A| = 2\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3\\ 0 & k \end{vmatrix} - (-1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 4 & k \end{vmatrix} + 0$

$= 2[1\cdot k - 0 \cdot 3] + 1[1\cdot k - 4\cdot 3]$
$= 2k + (k - 12)$
$= 3k - 12$

Set $3k - 12 = 0 \implies k = 4$.

Now, substitute $k=4$ in $B$.

$\det(B) = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$

Expand about $R_1$:
$1 \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} - 2\begin{vmatrix}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} + 3\begin{vmatrix}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$

$= 1(2\times 1 - 1\times 1) - 2(4\times 1 - 1\times 1) + 3(4\times 1 - 2\times 1)$
$= 1(2-1) -2(4-1) +3(4-2)$
$= 1(1) -2(3) +3(2)$
$= 1 -6 +6 = 1$

So, the answer is $1$.

Correct answer: (A) 1.
